stories.headline: A restaurant's video of a mother eating seven bowls of plain rice, and the kind owner who secretly slipped her ¥300, made China cry. The owner had staged the whole thing.
stories.what: Around 4 Nov a restaurant in Liangping, Chongqing posted a video: a mother and daughter order only a ¥6 plate of bean sprouts, the mother eats seven bowls of plain rice, and the owner, 'Sister Ying', quietly adds dishes to their bag with a note and ¥300 cash. It spread across Chinese platforms as a feel-good clip.
stories.twist: Viewers spotted logic holes and found the owner had posted a tearful video about her struggling business in May; a manager told reporters it was the shop's own promotion. On 12 Nov Liangping's joint investigation team said the video was staged: the 57-year-old operator, surnamed Li, invented the story for traffic, and a case was opened against her.
stories.why: The kindest person in the video was the only one acting.
stories.result: Verified (official notice via The Paper, Huxiu, China.com, Sina): case opened 12 Nov 2026. Sales effect unknown. Penalty unknown.
stories.note: Entertainment 8 · Narrative 7 · Business 7 · Evidence 7 · Freshness 9. Candidate, not a pick: no penalty yet, original Douyin post not found. Same family as last week's pick (staged banner videos).

stories.headline: Someone crushed a 7-Eleven egg sandwich on camera to advertise an Osaka sandwich shop. 4 million views later, the shop was apologising for an ad it says it never ordered.
stories.what: On 14 Nov a one-minute Instagram video showed a hand squeezing a packaged 7-Eleven egg sandwich flat, then cut to the kitchen of Dekasan, an Osaka shop known for oversized sandwiches: 'a sandwich this big should be illegal'. It passed 4 million views by 16 Nov (J-CAST).
stories.twist: The backlash hit the shop: food waste, trashing a rival, bare hands with long nails on raw egg. On 15 Nov the shop apologised on X and said it never asked for, paid for or supplied the video; it says a customer made it and asked for deletion. The shop now requires gloves.
stories.why: A free ad turned into the shop's worst week, and the shop says it never asked for it.
stories.result: Reported via J-CAST, coki, Yahoo Japan: apology 15 Nov; 4M+ views. Sales impact unknown. Who made the video: unclear.
stories.dates: Video 14 Nov 2026 · apology 15 Nov · J-CAST 16 Nov 2026
